title: approval.v1: one approval request, as a client reads it
description: PUBLIC record. The core draws every approval, on every surface, from this record and from nothing else. approval_id is minted by the core, never by an engine or a plugin. source says where the request came from: 'engine_tool' (an engine asked permission for a tool call) or 'plugin_effect' (a plugin asked to carry out an effect). ONE RULE BINDS WHAT IS SHOWN TO WHAT IS APPROVED, and conformance/rules.py states it as code that the vectors in vectors/ check: (1) effect is exactly what is being approved. (2) digest is the SHA-256, in lower-case hex, of effect's canonical bytes in the form digest_form names. (3) rendered is the lines of that same effect in the form rendered_form names: every field of the effect is on a line, nothing else is, and nothing is ever cut. Render every variable effect member, including the bound session/log identity. All variable text, including cwd and plugin-effect fields, uses the same escaping and continuation-line encoder. Labels count toward the per-line maximum. Before committing an approval, validate the complete rendered record against both the semantic renderer and its schema. If the complete representation cannot fit, return the typed refusal and create no approval; never truncate. The record's envelope session/run identifiers must agree with those in its effect. A record whose digest is not the digest of its effect, or whose lines are not the lines of its effect, is not an approval, whatever a schema says of its shape. A surface prints the rendered lines in full, in order, and composes no approval text of its own. display is extra text for the reader (labels and values, in order). It is OUTSIDE the digest, each entry says whether it is trusted, and a surface shows it only after the rendered lines and apart from them: it never replaces, contradicts or hides a line of the effect. Nothing defaults to approve: a request nobody answers is 'expired' at expires_at, and expired means denied. REVISION. revision counts changes to the request's CONTENT: its effect, its rendered lines, its deadline. It starts at 1. A showing does not change it and neither does an answer: an answer changes the request's state, not its content. An opening carries the revision that was shown, so if the content ever changes, the revision rises and everyone must look again before an answer is taken. Content may change only while pending; every such change increments revision. Resolved effect, rendering and deadline are immutable. Execution consumes exactly the approved (approval_id, revision, digest) and its matching private engine binding, once. A cached successful answer never authorizes another revision or another dispatch. Build a proposed approval revision in a separate candidate. Validate the complete candidate's shape, canonical digest, rendered lines and envelope/effect identity before committing it. A failure is a typed refusal and leaves the prior record, revision and binding unchanged. Only a valid candidate replaces the pending record. Changing content is not permission to change the target through an inconsistent envelope. (The refusals are typed: 'target' for an effect bound to another run, session or engine, or from another plugin, than the one it replaces; 'timestamp' for a deadline that is not a real instant; the renderer's own code for an effect that cannot be drawn whole; and the first thing that does not agree inside the candidate otherwise.) What is carried out is a record that agrees with itself: consumption checks the whole record again and refuses one whose digest, lines or envelope are not its effect's, or whose call holds a number that is not normalised. THE PROTOCOL. approval.list returns summaries ($defs/summary) and does not count as showing anything. A surface calls approval.open when it actually displays the lines; that adds one entry to opened_by (the principal, the surface, the revision shown, the time) and returns this record. The same principal on the same surface at the same revision is recorded once; another surface adds its own entry and changes no other. approval.answer names the digest that was drawn and the revision it read. The order of its checks: the caller is an 'owner' or a 'device' (an engine, a plugin and a session token never are); the same command id with the same params returns the first answer. Before accepting a fresh answer, atomically compare the server's current time with expires_at. At or after the deadline, a pending request becomes expired with no answer/answerer/answered_at, and the fresh answer returns conflict with detail already_resolved. Expiration and answering are serialized with the request state. A replay of a prior receipt is historical and cannot dispatch an effect again. The checks then go on: a request that is no longer pending is 'conflict' (already_resolved), so the first valid answer wins; a revision that is not the current one, which means the content changed after the caller read it, is 'conflict' (stale_revision); a principal and surface with no opening at the current revision is 'prompt_not_shown'; a digest that is not this record's is 'conflict' (digest_mismatch). 'approved' becomes 'consumed' when the effect is carried out, once. 'vetoed' is a refusal that is final for that digest. No credential appears in this record. The daemon also keeps a private binding from the approval to the engine's own pending request ($defs/binding); it never leaves the daemon. DECIDED by the owner on Nov 13, 2026, and marked for follow-up research in case it needs to be reworked: an engine's call is bound under RFC 8785 ('rfc8785/v1'); plugin effects, and every signature that exists today, keep 'csl-cj/v0'. README.md has the profile in full. conformance/rules.py (ApprovalModel) states the protocol, the deadline, a change of content and the single consumption as code, and the vectors in vectors/approval.lifecycle walk them.

digest_form.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over (conformance/rules.py, effect_bytes). 'rfc8785/v1': the UTF-8 bytes of the whole effect written as RFC 8785 writes it; used for an engine's tool call. 'csl-cj/v0': the restricted canonical JSON of plugin_security/canonical.py; used for a plugin's effect, as the approval gate and every signature use it today. The name carries its version: a later form is a new name here, never a silent change.

rendered_form.description: The rule the rendered lines follow. 'csl-approval-lines/v0' is conformance/rules.py, approval_lines: a line of the core's own words is trusted; a line that carries anything an engine or a plugin supplied is untrusted, and that text is written as JSON text, quotes included, with every character a surface must never be handed raw (controls, the marks that reorder or hide text, private use and the like: rules.py, NOT_SHOWN_RAW) written as a \u escape, so nothing can reorder, hide or forge part of a line and two different values never draw the same line. A later rule is a new name here, never a silent change.

rendered.description: The lines of the effect, in the form rendered_form names. Every surface prints exactly these lines. For an engine's tool call: a header, the engine, the session the call is bound to (the word none for a run that has no session), the run, the tool, the directory, the number of input fields, then each field of the input as its key and its value. For a plugin's effect: a header, then every field of the effect, then each field of the payload. Every line that carries an engine's or a plugin's text, the directory and each field of a plugin's effect included, goes through one encoder: a line holds at most 4,000 characters of it, the label included, and the rest continues on lines that start with two spaces, so no line is longer than this schema allows. An effect that would need more than 200 lines is never drawn and never approved: the core denies it without asking.

opened_by.description: Every showing of the request that approval.open recorded: who, on which surface, which revision of the request's content was shown, and when. One entry for each principal, surface and revision; a later opening by another surface adds an entry and removes none. Adding an entry does not change the revision.

state.description: pending: nobody has answered. approved: answered 'approve'; the effect may be carried out once. consumed: it was carried out. denied: answered 'deny'. vetoed: refused, and final for that digest. expired: the deadline passed with no answer, which means denied.

summary.description: What approval.list returns for each request: enough to list it and to count down its deadline, and nothing that could be taken for the prompt itself. Reading a summary is not showing the request.

surface.description: The kind of surface that drew the request.

approver.description: Who answered. Only the owner or a paired device may.

engine_tool_effect.description: An engine asked permission for one tool call. kind, engine, session_id and run_id are the core's own. tool, cwd and input are what the engine supplied: the tool's name, the directory the call would run in (null when the engine does not say) and the tool's input, an object the core never interprets. All three are held to one strict profile (conformance/rules.py: read_strict, check_call), which a schema cannot state in full and the vectors in vectors/call.profile hold case by case. Reading what the engine sent: the input is JSON text and an object; an object that names a key twice, at any depth, is refused, never resolved to the first or the last; NaN and the infinities are refused; half of a surrogate pair on its own is refused; nesting stops at 64; strings are kept exactly as written, with no Unicode normalisation. NUMBERS. Admission does not depend on a JSON number's lexical spelling or the host language's integer/float distinction. An integral numeric value outside -(2^53-1)..2^53-1 is refused as integer_out_of_range, including fraction or exponent spellings; this check is made before lossy conversion. A conversion that produces an out-of-range integral binary64 value is also refused. Other admitted numbers are finite binary64 values. Unsupported exact quantities and identifiers must be represented as strings. Canonicalizing and re-reading any admitted call must yield an admitted call with the same canonical bytes. The normalized bound numeric value, including -0 normalized to +0, is the value dispatched. A permission-only bridge that cannot replace the input must establish that its pending request has these same numeric semantics before granting it; pending-request identity alone is insufficient. Exact numeric range checks are independent of the host Decimal context and never escape as host arithmetic exceptions. Every integral value outside the safe range, including 1e1000000, is refused as integer_out_of_range. Before creating, changing or restoring a bound engine-tool effect, normalize its numeric values under this profile. Already-bound-effect validation and consumption must reject a nonnormalized effect; successful call-text parsing is not the only enforcement boundary. Digesting, rendering and dispatch use that same normalized value. This does not change csl-cj/v0 plugin effects or existing signature formats. (In conformance/rules.py: read_strict, normalised, unnormalised, check_call and effect_bytes; a held call or effect that carries an integral float or minus zero is refused as not_normalised, and the vectors approval.binding/x19 and approval.lifecycle/s11 hold both sides.) The tool's name and the directory are text under the same rules: any alphabet, no half pair, nothing normalised. What is bound: the digest is taken over the UTF-8 bytes of the WHOLE effect as RFC 8785 writes it (keys in the order of their UTF-16 code units; numbers as ECMAScript writes them, so 1.0 is 1 and 1e-7 is 1e-7; strings as themselves), so the core's fields and the engine's are under one form. Size, PROVISIONAL: tool, cwd and input together, as RFC 8785 writes them, are at most 262,144 bytes of UTF-8, and the approval's lines at most 200. A call that does not fit is refused with a typed code ('too_large', 'too_many_lines') and is never truncated: no request is drawn and the engine is told the call was denied. What is carried out is the call that was bound: where an engine's permission protocol lets the answer carry the input, the driver sends back the bound input, and otherwise the private binding to the engine's own pending request is the link. Only the approvals lane reads an effect; a surface prints the rendered lines.

plugin_effect.description: A plugin asked to carry out an effect: the 'csl-effect/vNext' object the approval gate already checks (plugin_security/approval.py). scope names the account, venue, contract family, adapter and environment, so a paper effect and a live one have different digests. amount_minor is in whole minor units of currency. payload is the plugin's own data; the core never interprets it, and draws each of its fields as its key and the text of its value.

binding.description: PRIVATE. Never sent to any client and never written to the event log. What the daemon keeps so that an answer reaches the right pending request of the right engine: the approval, the run, and the engine's own id for its permission request. The effect is carried out against exactly the approved approval_id, revision and digest and this binding, once: after that the request is 'consumed', and a second attempt, or one with another binding, is refused. For an engine-tool approval, the private binding's approval_id, run_id and engine must equal the approved record's approval_id, the record/effect run_id, and the effect's engine. These equalities are checked after recovery as well as on first consumption. A mismatch returns binding_mismatch and changes neither approval state nor consumption state. Equality with an internally retained binding object alone is insufficient. Consumption still requires the exact approved revision and digest and occurs at most once. A plugin's effect has no pending request of an engine: the daemon keeps no binding for it and none is offered, and it is carried out once against its approval, revision and digest. A driver answers the engine only through this binding; engine output can neither open nor answer an approval. No credential appears here.
